Industry insurance

Insurance for Hotels and Hospitality Businesses in Kenya

Hospitality businesses operate around guests, property, food, employees, equipment and changing occupancy. A suitable insurance programme should reflect the actual premises, services, assets and contractual responsibilities-not just a generic business package.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

Risks to consider

Property damage

Fire, water damage and other insured events can damage buildings, furniture, equipment, kitchens and stock.

Business interruption

A major insured loss may interrupt operations and revenue while repairs or recovery take place.

Guest and public liability

Guests, visitors and third parties may allege injury or property damage connected with the business.

Employee exposures

Staff injuries, medical needs and employment-related obligations should be considered.

Food, equipment and operations

Kitchen equipment, refrigeration, food handling and operational exposures may need specific consideration.

Insurance covers to discuss

  • Property and fire insurance
  • Business interruption, where available and appropriately arranged
  • Public liability
  • WIBA and employers-related covers
  • Machinery breakdown and electronic equipment
  • Burglary and money
  • Motor and goods in transit where relevant

What to have ready

  • Buildings and improvements
  • Furniture, fixtures and equipment
  • Kitchen and refrigeration equipment
  • Stock and consumables
  • Payroll and employee numbers
  • Guest facilities and activities
  • Annual revenue and expected recovery period
  • Claims history

The appropriate cover depends on your activities, policy terms, insurer underwriting and availability. This page is general information, not a guarantee that any particular risk is covered.
